segments.text: Does the Sun ever take a breath?
In the past 400 years the solar constant has varied less than 0.2 percent.
Each of the last three 11‑year sunspot cycles nudged it by about 0.1 percent.
Longer cycles also appear: the 11‑year Schwabe, the ~88‑year Gleisberg, the ~208‑year DeVries, and the ~1,000‑year Eddy cycles.
Researchers identify these rhythms from sunspot counts and cosmogenic radionuclide records.
All of these shifts are modest, on the order of a few tenths of a percent, yet they still alter the Sun’s output.
